cases.question: What is the mandatory spindle bearing lubrication interval and lubricant specification for the CNC Milling Center?
cases.expected_answer: Spindle bearing lubrication is mandatory every 250 operating hours using synthetic ISO VG 68 lubricant.
expected_facts: Spindle bearing lubrication is mandatory every 250 operating hours using synthetic ISO VG 68 lubricant.
cases.ground_truth_evidence: Section 2.1: Spindle bearing lubrication is mandatory every two hundred and fifty (250) operating hours using synthetic ISO VG 68 lubricant.
cases.evaluation_criteria: Must specify 250 operating hours and ISO VG 68 lubricant.

cases.question: What is the required operational overlap duration during shift handover and who must sign the logbook?
cases.expected_answer: A 30-minute operational overlap is enforced at every shift change, and both outgoing and incoming shift leads must conduct a joint walk-through and sign the electronic Shift Handover Log (SHL).
expected_facts: A 30-minute operational overlap is enforced at every shift change, and both outgoing and incoming shift leads must conduct a joint walk-through and sign the electronic Shift Handover Log (SHL).
cases.ground_truth_evidence: Section 1.2: A thirty (30) minute operational overlap is enforced at every shift change. Outgoing and incoming shift leads must conduct a joint walk-through inspection and sign the electronic Shift Handover Log (SHL).
cases.evaluation_criteria: Must state 30 minutes overlap and signed by outgoing and incoming shift leads.

cases.question: What is the dimensional tolerance for high-precision aerospace components versus automotive components?
cases.expected_answer: High-precision aerospace components require tolerances within +/- 0.025 mm, while standard automotive components require tolerances within +/- 0.050 mm.
expected_facts: High-precision aerospace components require tolerances within +/- 0.025 mm, while standard automotive components require tolerances within +/- 0.050 mm.
cases.ground_truth_evidence: Section 3.1: High-precision aerospace components require dimensional tolerances within +/- 0.025 mm. Standard commercial and automotive components require dimensional tolerances within +/- 0.050 mm.
cases.evaluation_criteria: Must specify +/- 0.025 mm for aerospace and +/- 0.050 mm for automotive.

cases.question: What surface finish roughness threshold is mandatory for critical bearing seats?

cases.evaluation_criteria: Must list all 6 LOTO steps in correct sequence.

expected_facts: Minimum safety stock is two (2) units for critical ceramic spindle bearings (Part # AIS-BRG-880) and five (5) units for pneumatic solenoid valves (Part # AIS-VAL-420).
cases.ground_truth_evidence: Section 5.1: two (2) units for critical ceramic spindle bearings (Part # AIS-BRG-880) and five (5) units for pneumatic solenoid valves (Part # AIS-VAL-420).
cases.evaluation_criteria: Must state 2 units for bearings and 5 units for valves.

cases.question: What is the standard procurement lead time for domestic replacement tooling versus imported CNC servomotors?
cases.expected_answer: Domestic replacement cutting tooling carries a lead time of 14 business days, while imported Japanese CNC servomotors carry 45 business days.
expected_facts: Domestic replacement cutting tooling carries a lead time of 14 business days, while imported Japanese CNC servomotors carry 45 business days.
cases.ground_truth_evidence: Section 5.3: Domestic replacement cutting tooling carries a standard lead time allowance of fourteen (14) business days. Imported Japanese CNC servomotors carry a lead time allowance of forty-five (45) business days.
